one_liner: Pure-Rust, no_std TrueType/OpenType glyph rasterizer and simple layout; first-party plots show 2.3x-11x lower per-glyph latency than FreeType.
what_it_does: Fontdue parses a .ttf/.otf/.ttc once into its own owned structures (Font::from_bytes) and then returns metrics plus an 8-bit coverage bitmap per character or glyph index (rasterize, rasterize_indexed, and a horizontal-subpixel variant that renders at 3x width). A separate, explicitly naive Layout type positions left-to-right text with word or letter wrapping. It targets the rusttype/ab_glyph/glyph_brush_layout niche, not FreeType's API: no shaping, no hinting, no colour or bitmap glyphs.
how_it_is_fast: Most work is moved to load time: every glyph reachable from cmap (and GSUB when load_substitutions is on) is outlined through ttf-parser, curves are flattened by midpoint subdivision with a triangle-area tolerance tied to FontSettings.scale, lines are re-based to the glyph bounding box with orientation fixed and reciprocal slopes precomputed. Per call it only scales those lines and runs a font-rs style signed-area accumulation rasterizer: each line walks the pixels it crosses (a separate path for vertical lines) and adds coverage deltas into an f32 buffer with unchecked indexing, then one prefix-sum pass converts the buffer to 8-bit coverage, four lanes at a time with SSE shift-adds, truncating converts and saturating packs into an output vector that is not zero-initialised. There is no hinting and no per-call table parsing; char-to-glyph lookup is a hashbrown HashMap.
when_to_use: Rust games, immediate-mode GUIs or wasm apps that rasterize Latin-like glyphs on demand into a glyph atlas, load a font once, and care about per-glyph latency.
no_std + alloc targets (embedded, wasm) that need TTF/OTF grayscale coverage without linking FreeType or another C library.
Replacing rusttype or ab_glyph plus glyph_brush_layout where simple left-to-right wrapping without kerning or shaping is acceptable.
Rendering at one or a few known sizes: building a Font with FontSettings.scale equal to that size reproduces the setup behind the README plots.
when_not_to_use: Complex scripts, running-text ligatures or bidi: there is no shaping (the README points to Cosmic Text) and the layout is self-described as naive.
Crisp small UI text: no hinting of any kind, and open issues #162 and #168 report blurry text at small sizes.

Large CJK fonts or tight memory: every mapped glyph is parsed and flattened at load (fast load is a stated non-goal); #164 links a Slint report of a 170 MB memory difference with a 28,987-glyph Chinese font.

Untrusted font files in a hardened process: a transmute-to-char UB on crafted cmap data (#172) was fixed only in 0.9.4 (2026-07-29), the rasterizer relies on unchecked writes over sanitised geometry, and a fuzzing-harness PR (#17) has been open since April 2020.
Colour emoji, embedded bitmap strikes, variable-font axes (#121, no API) or a C/C++ codebase: unsupported, and the API is Rust-only with no C ABI.

integration.dependencies: ttf-parser 0.25 (opentype-layout, no-std-float); hashbrown 0.15 by default (or the std feature for std::HashMap); optional rayon 1.10 for the parallel feature (threaded font loading)
integration.min_toolchain: Not documented: no rust-version in Cargo.toml (edition 2018); the default hashbrown 0.15 dependency declares Rust 1.63
integration.platforms: Any target with alloc (no_std); SSE/SSE2 intrinsics on x86 and x86-64 with the default simd feature, scalar fallback elsewhere (aarch64, wasm)
integration.thread_safety: Font is documented as immutable after creation and owns all its data (Vec and HashMap, no lifetimes), so it can be shared across threads by Rust's auto traits; Layout is mutated through &mut and should be one per thread.

gotchas: FontSettings.scale (default 40 px) fixes the curve-flattening tolerance at load: per the doc comment, smaller sizes render slightly slower and larger sizes look worse. The README plots built a separate Font per benchmarked size with scale equal to that size, so a single default Font will not match them at 10 px or 200 px.
rasterize allocates a new f32 accumulation buffer and a new Vec<u8> on every call; cache results (layout's GlyphRasterConfig is the documented hashable key).
Kerning is read only from the legacy kern table (GPOS pair kerning is ignored, #161), and the Layout type applies no kerning at all.

Open #169 reports wrong glyphs for U+0080-U+00FF with Courier, Monaco and Menlo; from_bytes merges codepoints from every cmap subtable without checking whether the subtable is Unicode, which would let a Mac Roman subtable overwrite Latin-1 entries (my reading of src/font.rs; not confirmed by the maintainer). Separately, the name-table decoder (unicode::decode_utf16, called from from_bytes) still builds chars with from_u32_unchecked without validating surrogates: a name string that starts with a low surrogate yields a code point of 0x110000 or more, the same class of UB as #172.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick fontdue over TiTanF when you want the more widely used pure-Rust rasterizer (TiTanF's own README measures fontdue faster at 10-160 px) and over raw ttf-parser when you need bitmaps, not just outlines; font-rs is the project it was forked from and then rewritten. Pick Parley (or cosmic-text) instead whenever text needs shaping, bidi or real paragraph layout.
verified_claims_summary: First-party criterion plots last regenerated in September 2020 (CPU, rustc, flags and FreeType version unstated) time 37 glyphs of a pangram in Exo 2 at 10-200 px: roughly 3x faster than FreeType 2 (via freetype-rs) for TrueType and 11x for CFF at 10 px, 2.3x and 2.8x at 200 px, and 5.8x faster layout than glyph_brush_layout at 1000 characters (chart readings). The comparison favours fontdue: its parsing and flattening run at load outside the timed loop, while every FreeType iteration calls set_char_size and then parses, hints and renders each glyph. In current FreeType source that size request resets the auto-hinter and TrueType size state, and this TTF (no fpgm, 7-byte prep, maxSizeOfInstructions 0) meets ftobjs.c's rule for the auto-hinter. In the layout benchmark glyph_brush_layout does a kerning lookup per glyph pair and returns a new Vec per call, while fontdue reuses its Layout and applies no kerning.
status_note: Active but solo and slow-moving (Cargo badge 'experimental'): 0.9.4 on 2026-07-29 only fixed soundness issue #172, with 30 open issues and 7 open PRs; 9.2M crates.io downloads (2.3M recent) and an MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR Zlib licence make it easy to adopt in Rust, but it is not copyable into C++ without an FFI layer.
